D003-D008_h012.question_both: Lately, things have been… a lot. My wife says I’m bouncing off the walls, and I guess she’s right. I can’t sit still for a minute, even during staff meetings. It feels like this buzzing under my skin, like I have to be moving or doing *something*. It’s been happening for about a month now, maybe a bit longer. In class, I find myself jumping in when students are talking, or finishing their sentences. I know it’s rude, but the thought just pops out. I’ve also noticed I’m making more silly mistakes grading papers, missing things I usually catch. My principal even mentioned a few careless errors in my lesson plans last week. And waiting for anything, whether it’s the microwave or for my turn to speak, just drives me crazy. I just want to get on with it.
D003-D008_h012.question_a:
I'm 44, a high school teacher, and married. Lately, I can't sit still; it's like a constant motor running inside me. Even during faculty meetings, I’m fidgeting, tapping my foot, needing to move. It’s been happening for as long as I can recall, definitely since before I was 12. My wife gets frustrated because I constantly interrupt her and the kids, jumping into conversations and finishing their sentences without thinking. Waiting my turn is agony, whether it's in line at the grocery store or just letting a student finish their thought.

Sometimes, I do feel really upbeat, energetic, sort of "on top of the world" - maybe even a little irritable too. But this restlessness, the urge to move, that's just always there. It’s not like it suddenly kicks in only when I’m feeling really high. And honestly, it makes my work harder. The other day, I was grading papers and missed a whole section of a student's answer, just completely overlooked it, despite usually being so detail-oriented. It’s like my mind is always racing, and I make careless mistakes I shouldn't.
D003-D008_h012.question_b:
Lately, I’ve been feeling an undeniable surge of energy, like I could run a marathon and teach three classes afterwards without breaking a sweat. It's not just energy, though; it’s a constant restlessness that makes it hard to sit still, especially during faculty meetings. My wife has noticed it too, saying I'm constantly pacing or fidgeting.

It’s been spilling into everything. I find myself blurting things out, cutting off students and colleagues mid-sentence, and I just can’t seem to wait my turn in conversations anymore. I even interrupt my wife. She thinks I'm not listening, but it's like my thoughts are coming so fast, I have to get them out. This makes me rush through grading papers, leading to careless mistakes. It's all happening at once, this intensity, and it’s been going on for a few weeks now.

My wife, bless her heart, she’d have had a word or two about me constantly pacing the house, or getting up mid-meal. I just feel this persistent need to be moving, like there’s a motor running inside me that I can’t switch off. I find myself butting into conversations down at the community center, or interrupting people without even realizing it. My mind jumps from one thing to another, and I struggle to keep my focus on anything for long, whether it's reading the paper or trying to organize my old workshop. Everything feels a bit jumbled. I've also been feeling quite a bit more energized lately, almost buzzing, and finding I need much less sleep, but it’s not really making me feel good, just sort of…wired.
D003-D008_h025.question_a: "Well, doctor, it’s not really new, but it’s gotten to where it’s just too much to handle. Even as a kid, before I was 12, my teachers would always tell my parents I was fidgety and couldn’t sit still. I've always felt like I’m driven by a motor, even now in retirement. I find myself getting up and pacing the house constantly, even when I'm supposed to be relaxing. It's hard to follow a conversation sometimes, my mind just wanders, and I end up interrupting people without meaning to, just blurting things out. My late wife, bless her heart, used to say I was impossible to plan anything with because I’d always jump from one task to another, never quite finishing or organizing anything properly. Lately, I've had these surges of energy, almost like a high, feeling incredibly optimistic and full of big plans, even sleeping much less. But the restlessness and trouble focusing, that’s always there, no matter how I’m feeling. It’s been continuous, not just when these more intense moods come and go."
D003-D008_h025.question_b: I've been feeling so… wound up lately, doctor. It's not like me. Lately, I just can't sit still for a minute; feels like I'm buzzing, like a motor, always on the go. My wife, bless her soul, used to say I was a quiet man. But these past few weeks, it's like a switch flipped. I'll be in the middle of a conversation with my daughter, and before I know it, I’m cutting her off, blurting out whatever comes to mind. It's like I have to say it right then and there. I've even found myself just getting up and pacing during bridge games, even though everyone else is still seated. It’s not how I usually am. I've always been a bit slower, more methodical. This restless energy, this urge to just keep moving and interrupting, it only pops up when I get into these highly energetic moods. Otherwise, I’m pretty calm. It's just when these manic periods hit that everything gets chaotic.
